The Northern Lights may be visible across parts of the north tonight

22:30, 10 Oct 2026Updated 22:37, 10 Oct 2026

The Met Office has revealed where in the UK you could catch a glimpse of the Northern Lights tonight (October 10). The UK is set for 'fantastic viewing opportunities', according to the weather body.

‌

‌

Many people across the UK took to social media to post pictures of the lights - with images taken as far south as Leeds.

‌

It comes as temperatures in Greater Manchester are forecast to plunge as low as 6C over the coming week as the Met Office warns the UK is likely to see "frost" over the weekend.

‌

The Northern Lights are caused by large explosions of activity from the sun which throw out huge amounts of charged particles into space.

‌

When these particles are captured by the Earth's magnetic field, they can collide with gas molecules in the atmosphere in an event called a geomagnetic storm. These collisions give off energy as light, forming spectacular colourful displays in the sky.

While typically confined to northern latitudes, the Met Office says 'building geomagnetic activity' could make the aurora more visible in southern latitudes, including the UK.

Article continues below

The Met Office said on social media: "The Northern Lights may be visible across parts of the north tonight. With skies clearing in places, there could be some fantastic viewing opportunities."

Between October 10 and October 13 there will be possible daily sightings across Scotland and similar geomagnetic longitudes where skies are clear, according to the Met Office.

It said: "Two glancing coronal mass ejections followed by a coronal hole high speed stream bring a daily chance of enhancing the auroral oval, with sightings possible across Scotland and similar geomagnetic longitudes where skies are clear between 10-13 Oct."
